title: Weekly ops briefing playbook — Amar (personal)
content:
Purpose: quick, low-friction briefing for the weekly engineering check-in (serving runtime + infra + console). This is my single-page scratch playbook — terse, action-focused, and built to be copy-pasted into the meeting invite or Slack thread.

Format: 30m standing; round-robin highlights (2–3 min per lead), urgent items first, then 10m for decisions and action assignment. Keep deep technical dives to follow-ups.

Prep notes (things I will call out):
- Observability: recent trace correlation improvements — ask console team for confirmation that trace IDs now surface in 100% of error paths (not just 90%).
- Latency cliff: noticed 95th->99th jump when sequence length > 1024 on p4d. Bring up micro-batching experiment (h2-micro-batching) results and whether to enable for more routes.
- KV cache cold-start: hit-rate still ~0.64 for busy customers; propose a short cache-warming job for dedicated nodes during maintenance windows.
- Quantized fallback: we rolled out q4a to a small shard; request metrics on hallucination/regression for the last 48h (QA + evals).
- Autoscale policy: someone on infra should weigh in on the new burst policy (min 2 -> min 1) — concern about tail latency under scale-up.
- Customer telemetry: ACME corp saw throttling on 2026-03-08; share timeline and who is owning customer comms.

Agenda (compact):
1) Quick wins / blockers (5m) — rapid fire, only items needing attention.
2) Metrics flash (5m) — 95/99 latency, cost/unit, KV hit-rate delta. I will call out the 99th for gen routes + embedding SLOs.
3) Rollouts & experiments (8m) — q4a quantized rollout status, h2 micro-batching A/B, dedicated autoscale change request.
4) Console/observability asks (5m) — trace ID coverage, per-token cost drilldown per customer token streams.
5) Decisions & action assignment (5m) — capture owners + due dates.

Quick metrics to read out live:
- Global 95th gen latency: 310ms (last 24h)
- Global 99th gen latency: 1.42s (last 24h)
- KV cache hit-rate (prod busiest 20%): 0.64 -> target 0.75
- Cost per million tokens (hosted): $24.7 -> trending +3% week-over-week

Action items (live tracker) — copy to meeting minutes after assigned:
- [ ] Owner: Marco Nguyen — Run KV warmup job proposal and estimated window; POST results to #ops-bridge. Due: 2026-03-15. Linked: JIRA ENGINF-1423.
- [ ] Owner: Sara Patel — Quantized rollout evaluation: produce hallucination/regression delta table for q4a vs baseline (sampled prompts). Due: 2026-03-14.
- [ ] Owner: Amar Singh — Draft customer-facing incident timeline for ACME (root cause hypothesis + immediate mitigations). Due: 2026-03-13.
- [ ] Owner: Infra on-call (TBD) — Autoscale policy rollback plan (min1/min2 experiment) and safety knobs. Due: 2026-03-16.
- [ ] Owner: Console team — Confirm trace ID coverage and open PR for trace->log linking in UI. Due: 2026-03-17.
- [ ] Owner: SRE rotation — Run the sherpa traffic test against dedicated pools (5m spike) and post results. Due: 2026-03-14.

Notes / conversation starters (things to surface if time):
- Stability budget idea: allocate token budget for expensive prepops (warmups + micro-batches) and monitor unit economics. Can we model this as #cost-per-10k-tokens?
- Fallback strategy: propose a new lightweight policy that routes to q2-small when p99 > threshold rather than full fallback to CPU. Pros/cons?
- Console UX: a single click to toggle to 'customer view' showing per-route costs would unblock support; small feature but high impact for CS.

Unresolved questions I want answers to during/after the meeting:
- Does the micro-batching patch (h2) introduce any token duplication or ordering edge case in function-calling flows? If yes, pause.
- Is the observed 99th spike correlated with a specific customer vector (synthetic workload) or an infra problem?
- Do we have a canonical incident template for customer comms (docs show multiple variants)? Put link in follow-ups.

Follow-ups I will do immediately after the meeting:
- Paste action items into JIRA sub-tasks and ping owners.
- Post summary + links in #serving-runtime with TL;DR and who to contact for deep dives.
- Schedule 30m deep-dive with console + infra if trace coverage isn't confirmed.

Scratch space / ad-hoc notes (chaotic):
- PR to watch: github.com/redwood/console/pull/1120 (trace id UX)
- Temp experiment name: h2-micro-batching (A/B), control routes: gen-small/default; metric: p99 + cost/unit
- Slack: #serving-runtime, #ops-bridge, #console-ux
- Confluence: Serving Runtime - Playbooks -> "Rollout safety" section (need to update with quantized checklist)
- Quick checklist for owners when marking action done: summary + raw metrics + how to rollback (1-line).

Personal todo (post-week):
- Consolidate micro-batching results into a one-pager for next week.
- Draft a standard fallback policy template and circulate.

If time, open question to group: agree to a 2-week freeze window for large kernel changes around Black Friday-like customer events? (short discuss; poll if needed)

End of scratch playbook — will trim and publish to meeting thread before standup.
